name: Sugar
label: Creation Records
lede: Bob Mould was done with Virgin and wanted a band again. He built one in Athens, Georgia, named it after a sugar packet at a Waffle House, and made the NME's album of the year before the band was a year old.

eras.title: After Hüsker Dü, a drummer and a bassist
eras.text: Hüsker Dü was over, two solo records on Virgin were done, and Bob Mould was touring alone with a pile of new songs. He already knew the drummer: he had produced Malcolm Travis's band the Zulus. The bassist came from the Athens band Mercyland.

years.h: Mould produces the Zulus, Malcolm Travis on drums
years.p: The Boston band's 1989 album is produced by Bob Mould. [[Malcolm Travis|3cf1300c-5f13-43cd-972e-7e9b397d201f]] had been the drummer in [[Human Sexual Response|a277340f-36f1-4051-b2e2-26932b86c65e]] before the Zulus.

years.h: Virgin and Mould part ways; Mercyland breaks up
years.p: After Workbook and Black Sheets of Rain, Mould leaves Virgin Records and tours the world solo. In Athens, [[David Barbe|89b39101-f955-4155-81f3-7d7430754a1b]]'s band [[Mercyland|be24e988-26d2-449e-9d06-714a791ba9ec]], which he started in 1985, ends the same year.

eras.title: Thirty songs in a tire shop
eras.text: The trio worked up thirty songs in the back of a tire shop in downtown Athens and played their first show within weeks. By September the record was out on Rykodisc in America and Alan McGee's Creation in Britain, where it landed hardest.

years.h: A sugar packet at a Waffle House names the band
years.p: Rehearsing thirty songs in a downtown Athens tire shop, Mould, Barbe and Travis need a name. Mould spots a sugar packet on their table at a Waffle House.

years.h: Sugar's first show is at the 40 Watt Club in Athens
years.p: Bob Mould's new trio plays its first concert, at the Athens club, after weeks of rehearsing thirty songs.

years.h: 'Changes' goes out first in the UK, on Creation
years.p: Creation Records leads with 'Changes' as Sugar's first British single, a month before the album.

years.src: Wikipedia: Copper Blue · Wikipedia: Bob Mould · Wikipedia: Sugar
yt: 'If I Can't Change Your Mind' video
years.h: Copper Blue lands on Rykodisc and Creation
years.p: Recorded at The Outpost in Stoughton, Massachusetts, with [[Lou Giordano|a48692c1-a248-408a-bf5b-b613161a8b20]] co-producing. It goes to No. 10 in the UK and sells close to 300,000 copies, Mould's best seller.
years.xp:
Videos for 'Helpless' and 'If I Can't Change Your Mind' got heavy MTV play, and the British singles kept coming: 'A Good Idea', 'Helpless', then 'If I Can't Change Your Mind' in 1993, which reached No. 30.

Mould has credited the timing. "When Nevermind came out, that album changed the way people listen to music," he said, adding that without it he didn't know if Copper Blue "would have stood a chance in '92."

q: The last word in love songs and the full stop after heartbreak.
years.h: The NME names Copper Blue its album of the year
years.p: The British weekly gave the record 9/10 and then its top spot for 1992. In America it placed seventh in the Village Voice's Pazz & Jop poll.

eras.title: The evil twin, then a scorched first try
eras.text: Sugar followed the hit with the darker half of the same sessions, timed for Easter. The proper second album came hard: the first sessions were thrown out, and Mould rebuilt the record from his own parts outward.

years.h: Beaster, released in Holy Week, goes to No. 3 in Britain
years.p: Six songs and about 31 minutes from the Copper Blue sessions, heavier and closer to [[Hüsker Dü|5c4c90a4-539f-4101-83cf-301bc6a94e06]]. Mould called it the first album's "evil twin."
years.xp:
The religious imagery was deliberate, down to the release date before Easter, with songs called 'Judas Cradle' and 'JC Auto'. "Those are words that are not used lightly," Mould said of it.

Select gave it five stars. It outcharted Copper Blue in the UK, and 'Tilted' went to No. 48.

years.cap: Malcolm Travis, David Barbe and Bob Mould, Beaster press photo
years.h: Mould erases the Atlanta tapes and starts again
years.p: Unhappy with the sound of the first sessions in Atlanta, Sugar scraps them. Mould erases the master tapes and rebuilds the album backward: his own parts first, then Barbe and Travis, drums last.
years.xp: Mould described the new songs as "pretty punk rock" but "beautiful and really harmonic," and said he was off solos: "I'm really starting to hate guitar solos, so I'm trying to avoid them."

years.h: File Under: Easy Listening makes the UK top ten
years.p: Produced by Mould, it reaches No. 7 in Britain and No. 50 on the Billboard 200. Entertainment Weekly gave it an A; the NME, 9/10.

eras.title: Last stop, Sendai
eras.text: Three years after the 40 Watt, Sugar played its last show on the other side of the world. Barbe went home to his family and, in time, to a studio career; Mould went back to his own name.

years.cap: Sugar, File Under: Easy Listening press photo
years.h: Sugar plays its last show in Sendai, Japan
years.p: The tour ends in Sendai and so does the band. Barbe wants more time with his growing family; Travis joins [[Kustomized|baca8d31-cd6b-4460-8843-ee286ce9cbf3]]; Mould carries on solo.

years.h: The B-sides come out after the band is gone
years.p: Besides collects the flip sides from the British singles run, including songs Barbe had written for his side band Buzz Hungry.

eras.title: Producers, professors and a box of Sugar
eras.text: Barbe built one of the busiest studios in the South and ended up teaching the music business at the University of Georgia. Mould went back to Copper Blue in 2012 and played it top to bottom, and Edsel boxed up everything the band recorded.

years.h: Barbe opens Chase Park Transduction in Athens
years.p: Barbe co-founds the studio and produces records for [[Drive-By Truckers|8eae1e0a-1696-4532-9e3c-0a072217ef4c]], [[R.E.M.|ea4dfa26-f633-4da6-a52a-f49ea4897b58]] and k.d. lang. By 2011 he directs UGA's Music Business Certificate Program.

years.src: Wikipedia: Bob Mould · Wikipedia: Sugar · Wikipedia: File Under: Easy Listening
years.h: Mould plays Copper Blue start to finish on tour
years.p: Announced at a 2011 tribute concert at Walt Disney Concert Hall, the tour runs through the summer festivals alongside Mould's Silver Age. Edsel reissues the album with B-sides, a live set and the videos.

years.h: Edsel collects it all on five CDs
years.p: After the 5xLP A Box of Sugar in 2013, Complete Recordings 1992–1995 gathers the albums, singles and live sets.

eras.title: Love you even still
eras.text: Thirty years after Sendai, all three members came back for real: new songs, sold-out New York and London dates and a world tour. Barbe had already been opening Mould's solo shows.

years.h: An Instagram account called Sugar Copper Blue appears
years.p: Short archival concert clips, no captions. Mould, Barbe and Travis all follow it; Stereogum and BrooklynVegan start asking if the band is back.

years.cap: Sugar at Webster Hall, New York
years.h: Sugar reforms with 'House of Dead Memories'
years.p: The band's new website announces shows in New York and London for May 2026 and a first new song in three decades. A UK, Europe and US tour running to October 2026 follows.

years.h: Mould digs up a 2007 song: 'Long Live Love'
years.p: Written in Washington, D.C., in the Bush years, it goes on a BMG 7-inch with 'House of Dead Memories' on May 1.
years.xp: The Love You Even Still world tour gives $2 from every US ticket to the Trevor Project, and £2 or €2 per UK and European ticket to PLUS1, for LGBTQ+ causes.

years.cap: Sugar at the National Stadium, Dublin, May 2026
years.h: Sugar plays the O2 Forum in London, first of two nights
years.p: After sold-out New York dates, the London shows on May 23 and 24 open a tour through Ireland, Britain, Scandinavia and Europe in June, then North America from August to October.

years.h: Changes: The Story of Sugar premieres on YouTube
years.p: The band's own documentary goes up on its channel, with the new single 'Keep Looping' out around it.
